import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_2.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_users = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)   # Source3_3_0: ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']
df_movies = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # Source3_3_1: ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df_ratings = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0) # Source3_3_2: ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']

# Step 2: Analyze target schema and source schemas
# Target schema: ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float]

# Step 3: Join source tables to form the target table
# - df_ratings has user_id, movie_id, rating, timestamp
# - df_users has user_id, age, occupation (gender and zip not needed)
# - df_movies has movie_id, title (genres not needed)
# Join plan:
#   Join df_ratings with df_users on 'user_id' (left join to keep all ratings)
#   Join the result with df_movies on 'movie_id' (left join to keep all ratings)
# After join, select and cast columns to match target schema

# Step 4: Perform joins
df_joined = df_ratings.merge(df_users[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='left')
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_movies[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Step 5: Aggregate by 'title' and 'movie_id' to get average user_id, age, occupation, rating, timestamp
# According to hints:
# - user_id, age, occupation are float in target but integer in source, so average aggregation applies
# - rating and timestamp are float, average aggregation applies
# - movie_id is integer, keep as is (group by)
# - title is string, group by
# Group by columns: 'title', 'movie_id'
# Aggregations:
#   user_id: mean (float)
#   age: mean (float)
#   occupation: mean (float)
#   rating: mean (float)
#   timestamp: mean (float)

agg_df = df_joined.groupby(['title', 'movie_id'], as_index=False).agg({
    'user_id': 'mean',
    'age': 'mean',
    'occupation': 'mean',
    'rating': 'mean',
    'timestamp': 'mean'
})

# Step 6: Reorder columns to match target schema
# Target schema order: ['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
agg_df = agg_df[['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']]

# Step 7: Cast columns to target types explicitly
agg_df['title'] = agg_df['title'].astype(str)
agg_df['user_id'] = agg_df['user_id'].astype(float)
agg_df['age'] = agg_df['age'].astype(float)
agg_df['occupation'] = agg_df['occupation'].astype(float)
agg_df['movie_id'] = agg_df['movie_id'].astype(int)
agg_df['rating'] = agg_df['rating'].astype(float)
agg_df['timestamp'] = agg_df['timestamp'].astype(float)

# Step 8: Save the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/target_multisource_cot.csv"
agg_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2 with Source0 on user_id
df = pd.merge(source2, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join the result with Source1 on movie_id
df = pd.merge(df, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns of the target schema:
# title (string), user_id (float but unique id), age (float), occupation (float), movie_id (int)
# According to hints, group by columns must NOT be float, but user_id and age and occupation are float in target.
# However, user_id and movie_id are identifiers, and title is string.
# The target examples show user_id as float, but it is an identifier, so we include it.
# We group by title, user_id, age, occupation, movie_id to aggregate rating and timestamp by mean.

group_cols = ["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id"]

# Aggregate rating and timestamp by mean
agg_dict = {
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean"
}

df_grouped = df.groupby(group_cols, as_index=False).agg(agg_dict)

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_grouped = df_grouped[["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"]]

# Write output
df_grouped.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_3/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
